articles.author: frank chu
articles.description:
Two days ago I wrote up the eMudhra incident: eight of the CA's intermediate private keys turned out to be integers smaller than 256 — I recovered all eight in 11 milliseconds, the largest was 237. Today eMudhra announced it is leaving the global SSL/TLS certificate business entirely (press release, Bengaluru, October 22; 894 points on Hacker News). A CA whose keys fit in a uint8 has decided certificates aren't worth it. Fair enough. But "a CA exits the business" is a press-release sentence, not a technical event — so I checked the three places where an exit would actually have to happen: your trust store, Mozilla's revocation list, and the incident record.
First, what the company says, in its own release: it revoked the affected CAs within 14 hours of discovery; no end-entity certificates…
articles.title: eMudhra quit the CA business today. I checked your trust store — its roots are still in it.

articles.author: frank chu
articles.description:
OpenShell — NVIDIA's "safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents" — hit the Hacker News front page today (257 points; the repo is at 17,719 stars, v0.1.5 shipped October 20). Most agent sandboxes sell you enforcement: Landlock, seccomp, a network proxy. OpenShell sells those too, but its headline differentiator is the second half: formal verification. Before a policy change is applied, an SMT-based prover checks what the change would allow.
That prover ships as a standalone CLI, openshell-prover, whose job is a boundary check: given a candidate policy and a boundary policy (the most access an environment allows), decide whether the candidate stays inside the boundary — and if not, produce a counterexample. The docs say the CLI is "primarily intended for agents": a parent agen…
articles.title: I built OpenShell's Z3 policy prover and ran 29 checks. It caught everything except the metadata address.

For large training artifacts sent from a browser, use presigned multipart uploads when you can own a three-state record in your database: uploading, retained, and deletion_due. Choose tus or UploadThing when polished interruption recovery matters more than a small storage contract; choose AWS S3 when versioning, Object Lock, or deeper native governance is mandatory.

강등 규칙을 빼고 총점만으로 줄을 세우면 시즌 1의 상위 50위 중 38개가 강등 대상이고, 원점수 1위(85.90점)는 공식 1위(84.72점)보다 높습니다. 순위표는 점수만이 아니라 필터로도 만들어집니다.

articles.author: The Block Research
articles.description:
Layer 2 scaling solutions help blockchains like Ethereum process more activity without forcing every transaction to happen directly on the base chain.
Ethereum’s main network is secure and decentralized, but blockspace is limited. When demand rises, fees increase and users can get priced out. Layer 2s address this by moving transaction activity to scaling systems that sit around Ethereum while still using it for settlement, security, data posting, or verification.
The most important Layer 2 designs today are rollups. Rollups process transactions off-chain, bundle them together, and post data or proofs back to Ethereum. This makes transactions cheaper and faster while keeping a connection to Ethereum’s trust foundation.
articles.title: Layer 2 Scaling Solutions
